text:
aisha: Hi @people-ops — heads up: two ICs on my team are expecting overlapping parental leave windows in July/Aug. Need a short, actionable plan: what paperwork to start now, how to handle coverage (temp contractor vs rotating on-call), and any payroll/benefits edge cases we should flag. Trying to lock this before headcount planning.

people-ops: Thanks, Aisha. Short checklist to start now: 1) Parental Leave Request form submitted by employees, 2) Verify FMLA/state eligibility, 3) Enroll in company pay-topup (if eligible) with payroll cutoff awareness, 4) Add beneficiary/K1 for benefits continuation if needed. Aim for 30 days notice; exceptions are okay. Form link: https://hr.redwood.example/forms/parental-leave

payroll: Quick items: company top-up enrollments must be submitted before payroll close for the pay period containing the first paid week (payroll cutoff is the 15th). If documentation (birth/adoption) comes late, we can do retro adjustments but expect a delay of 1-2 payroll cycles. For overlap, we model combined payment streams to avoid duplication with state benefits (CA/PFL, NYS). Send estimated dates now and final docs within 30 days.

jonathan: Thanks. For coverage options I'm leaning toward a 6-week contractor to cover maintenance and paging, plus an internal rotation for feature work. How quickly can we spin a short-term contractor?

hiring-ops-bot: Fast-track short-term contractor flow: 1) manager headcount approval + scoping note, 2) hourly cap and preferred vendors, 3) procurement routing. Typical timeline: 10-18 business days for SOW + background checks. Mark ticket as "urgent-temp" to prioritize.

emily: I can prep concise runbooks for the day-to-day and the oncall playbook. I'll record two 10-min Looms for deploy/run steps. Recommend pairing sessions last two weeks before leave.

people-ops: Sample coverage timeline you can adapt:
```
Week -2 to 0: runbook creation + pair shadowing
Week 1-2: contractor onboarding + ramp with shadowing
Week 3-8: contractor handles oncall + routine ops; team focuses on backlog
```

aisha: Good template. Any nuance about health insurance / COBRA or flexible spending accounts when both go out?

people-ops: Health: Active benefits continue while on paid company leave. If someone goes unpaid after company top-up and state benefits, they remain eligible for continuation; payroll will flag if COBRA paperwork is needed. FSAs are post-tax elections — check plan docs for mid-year changes; benefits@redwood.example can advise on FSA suspension or carryover.

payroll: One more pay gotcha: if both employees take overlapping paid leave and both claim the same dependent care benefits in a supplemental program, we need to check tax implications. We'll run a projection once you give dates.

jonathan: I'll ask both to submit their Parental Leave Request this week and share tentative start/end. Can people-ops open the hiring ops ticket so I can include hourly cap?

hiring-ops-bot: Ticket created: HR-TEMP-4567 (internal). Please add: max hourly rate, role summary (2-3 bullet points), and preferred start date. Procurement cc'd.

emily: I'll drop the runbook PR in the infra repo and tag jonathan/aisha for review. Also scheduling three 1-hr handoff sessions next Mon/Wed/Fri.

aisha: Perfect. Thanks team — I'll post dates here when both confirm. If the contractor timeline looks long, we may swap to full internal rotation and extend pairing.

people-ops: Happy to advise on rotation templates if needed; we can share a manager handoff doc and a compressed shadowing checklist. Link: https://hr.redwood.example/checklists/manager-handoff :sparkles:

payroll: Send estimated paystubs and dates to payroll@redwood.example and we'll return a combined-pay projection within 2 business days.

jonathan: Will do. Thanks everyone.
